question: True or false: landing a Falcon 9 booster for reuse costs less than a tenth of the payload it could otherwise lift?
answer: False. The booster must hold back fuel to turn or brake, re-enter and land, and carry legs and grid fins, so it lets the upper stage go at a lower speed. SpaceX has listed 8.3 tonnes to a high transfer orbit expended against 5.5 tonnes landed: a third of the payload left behind.
move: Every way back has to be paid for on the way out.
trap: Picturing the landing as a last small puff of spare fuel.
reference: SpaceX, Falcon 9 vehicle page, payload to geosynchronous transfer orbit, expendable and reusable, spacex.com/vehicles/falcon-9, 2023
